We need to extract triplets.

Entities: Cincinnati (city), John Cranley (person), Vice Mayor Christopher Smitherman (person with title), Councilmembers: Tamaya Dennard (President Pro-Tem), David Mann, Amy Murray, Chris Seelbach, P.G. Sittenfeld, Greg Landsman, Jeff Pastor, Wendell Young. City manager Harry Black. Assistant city managers (unspecified number, but we can note that manager maintains two assistant city managers). Relations: "position held" maybe "mayor of". Use relation like "head of government" or "position held". We'll follow typical Wikidata style: "head of government" for mayor? Actually mayor is "head of government" of city. Could use "position held". We'll use "position held" relation.

Triplets:

1. (John Cranley, position held, Mayor of Cincinnati) subject_type human, object_type political office? maybe "position". Use object "Mayor of Cincinnati". Could also separate as (John Cranley, office, Mayor) with qualifier location Cincinnati. But simpler: object "Mayor of Cincinnati". object_type "political office".

2. (Cincinnati, head of government, John Cranley) maybe reverse. But we can include both.

3. (Christopher Smitherman, position held, Vice Mayor of Cincinnati). Also note he's Vice Mayor.

4. (Tamaya Dennard, position held, Councilmember of Cincinnati) with qualifier "role" President Pro-Tem? Actually President Pro-Tem is a role within council. Could add qualifier: relation "position held" object "Councilmember of Cincinnati" qualifiers: {"relation":"position qualifier","object":"President Pro-Tem"} but need proper relation. Use qualifier "qualifier" maybe "position qualifier". We'll use "qualifier" relation "position qualifier". object "President Pro-Tem". object_type "title".

Similarly for other councilmembers without qualifier.

5-11: each councilmember position held.

6. (Harry Black, position held, City manager of Cincinnati).

7. (Harry Black, maintains, Assistant city manager) with qualifier "quantity" "two". But qualifiers are relations to object. Could have qualifier relation "quantity" object "2". object_type "quantity". Or we could have object "assistant city manager" and qualifier quantity 2.

Also maybe (Cincinnati, has council member, ...) but not needed.

Let's list.

Need subject_type and object_type.

Define types: human, political office, council member (maybe "political office").

Assistant city manager is a position.

We'll produce qualifiers list.

For councilmembers: object "Councilmember of Cincinnati". object_type "political office". For Tamaya Dennard, qualifier: {"relation":"position qualifier","object":"President Pro-Tem"} object_type "title". We'll set object_type for qualifier maybe "title". But qualifier format expects relation and object only, not object_type. So we just include relation and object.

For the "maintains" relation: relation "maintains", object "assistant city manager". qualifier: {"relation":"quantity","object":"2"}.

Now produce JSON.
